Since `h` comes from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting (admin-supplied free-form text), any value containing a single quote or SQL metacharacters would break the INSERT or inject SQL. The finding accurately describes the mechanism and it is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds an INSERT statement via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. `h` comes from `site_settings.value` split by newlines and is not escaped/quoted safely, so a host containing a single quote will break the SQL, and crafted content could inject SQL during migration. No normalization/sanitization is applied before insertion (the model’s `before_validation` won’t run for raw SQL inserts).
